concepts.title: Natural Magnets and Magnetite
concepts.definition: Naturally occurring rocks containing iron that have the inherent property of attracting iron pieces.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Magnetite is a natural magnetic mineral discovered in ancient times.
question_patterns: How was the first natural magnet discovered?
What is magnetite and what does it contain?
Who discovered natural magnets and where?
What is a natural magnet?
why is natural magnets and magnetite important

solution_steps.explain: Verify if the material is a naturally occurring iron-rich rock (magnetite).
Check if it naturally attracts iron objects without any artificial treatment.
Confirm the rock is magnetite (Fe3O4), an iron oxide mineral known since ancient times as lodestone, the first natural magnet.

concepts.title: Magnetic and Non-Magnetic Materials
concepts.definition: Classification of substances using whether they are attracted to a magnet (magnetic, like iron, nickel, cobalt) or not (non-magnetic, like plastic, wood, paper).
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Only specific metals and their alloys are indeed attracted to magnets.
question_patterns: Classify the following materials as magnetic or non-magnetic
Why is a pencil sharpener attracted to a magnet despite its plastic body?
Is cobalt a magnetic material?
What is the difference between magnetic and non-magnetic substances?
state two key points about magnetic and non-magnetic materials

solution_steps.explain: Bring a magnet close to the given object or material.
Observe if there is an attractive force pulling the object toward the magnet.
Classify as magnetic if attracted (e.g., iron, nickel, cobalt) or non-magnetic if not attracted.

concepts.title: Poles of a Magnet
concepts.definition: The regions near the two ends of a magnet where its magnetic strength is concentrated and attraction is strongest.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Every magnet has two poles, both North and South, located near its ends.
question_patterns: Where is the magnetic strength of a bar magnet strongest?
What are the poles of a magnet?
How can you find the location of poles on a magnet using iron filings?
Do poles exist in magnets of all shapes?
why is poles of a magnet important

solution_steps.explain: Spread iron filings uniformly on a flat sheet of paper.
Place the magnet on the sheet and observe where the filings accumulate.
Identify the regions of maximum accumulation at the ends as the magnetic poles.

concepts.title: Directive Property of a Freely Suspended Magnet
concepts.definition: A magnet hung freely so it can swing settles pointing along the geographic north-south line.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: A suspended magnet acts as a natural compass pointing North-South.
question_patterns: In which direction does a freely suspended bar magnet always align?
How can you find the North pole of an unmarked bar magnet?
Why does a suspended magnet point in a specific direction?
Describe the directive property of a magnet.
how does directive property of a freely suspended magnet work

solution_steps.explain: Suspend a bar magnet freely from its center using a thread so it can rotate without obstruction.
Let the magnet come to rest away from any draft or magnetic materials.
Identify the end pointing towards geographic North as the North pole, and the opposite end as the South pole.

concepts.title: The Magnetic Compass
concepts.definition: A navigation instrument consisting of a small, freely pivoted magnetic needle inside a dial marked with directions, used to find geographic directions.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: The pivoted needle aligns with the Earth's magnetic field to show the North-South direction.
question_patterns: How does a compass help in finding directions?
Describe the construction of a magnetic compass.
Why is the north pole of a compass needle painted in a different color?
How do you use a compass to find the East-West direction?
justify why the magnetic compass matters

solution_steps.explain: Place the compass on a flat surface at the location where directions need to be determined.
Wait for the magnetized needle to stop oscillating and come to rest in the North-South direction.
Rotate the compass casing until the 'N' and 'S' markings on the dial align with the ends of the needle.

concepts.title: Making an Artificial Magnet (Single-Touch Method)
concepts.definition: A method of magnetizing an iron piece by repeatedly stroking it with one pole of a bar magnet along its length in a single, continuous direction.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: An ordinary iron strip can be turned into a temporary magnet using a permanent magnet.
question_patterns: How can you make an iron strip into a magnet?
Explain the single-touch method of magnetization.
What precautions should be taken while making an artificial magnet?
How to magnetize an iron needle?
justify why making an artificial magnet (single-touch method) matters

solution_steps.explain: Place the iron strip flat on a table.
Drag one pole of a bar magnet along the strip from one end to the other.
Lift the magnet and return to the starting point, repeating this stroke 30-40 times in the same direction with the same pole.
Verify magnetization by bringing iron filings or pins near the strip.

concepts.title: Magnetic Attraction and Repulsion
concepts.definition: The fundamental law of magnetism stating that like magnetic poles repel each other, while unlike magnetic poles attract each other.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: North-both both North and South-South repel; North-South and South-North attract.
question_patterns: What happens when two similar poles of magnets are brought close?
What is the rule of attraction and repulsion between magnetic poles?
Will a North pole attract or repel another North pole?
How do opposite poles of two magnets interact?
what do you understand by magnetic attraction and repulsion

solution_steps.explain: Identify the poles of the two interacting magnets (North and South).
Compare the facing poles: if they are identical (N-N or S-S), they repel.
If the facing poles are different (N-S or S-N), they attract.

concepts.title: Care and Storage of Magnets
concepts.definition: Guidelines to prevent demagnetization, which occurs when magnets are indeed heated, hammered, dropped, or stored improperly without magnetic keepers.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Proper handling and keepers preserve magnetic properties over time.
question_patterns: How do magnets lose their magnetic properties?
How should bar magnets be stored safely?
What are the precautions to keep magnets from getting weak?
Why should magnets be kept away from electronic devices like mobiles and computers?
describe care and storage of magnets with an example

solution_steps.explain: Avoid physical abuse such as heating, hammering, or dropping the magnet.
Store bar magnets in pairs with opposite poles adjacent, separated by wood, and with soft iron keepers across their ends.
Keep magnets away from magnetic storage and electronic devices (CDs, computers, phones).
